final_v3_first_use_observation.hypothesis: DeepGEMM execute resolves a variant for actual M and calls ensure_compiled, so unseen-shape setup/JIT is a possible contributor. Existing logs contain no per-stage trace proving causality.
final_v3_first_use_observation.limit: Selected-schedule strict replay does not establish that every dynamic shape was prepared or that all provider JIT/setup is absent. Provider/native caches are shared and were not cleared; these two observations are not a controlled performance A/B.
final_v3_first_use_observation.observed: The first s24 prefill in strict replay is much slower than the same shape in the subsequent instrumented process; selected artifact remained unchanged in both.

final_v3_serving.selected_plan_findings: Decode off selects GenericMatmul LM head while on selects cuBLASLt; prefill heads have identical cuBLASLt descriptors. On decode has no multi-consumer activation sharing; prefill removes 48 of 400 activation quantizations. Variant choices also differ, so the whole-plan timing delta is not an isolated sharing estimate.

limitations: All B1 latency numbers include diagnostic logits. They are not serving throughput or TPOT. Instrumented CUDA Graph step intervals carry event overhead and are a separate metric.
B1 control/shared use the same binary but independent searched schedules. The LM head changes GenericMatmul to GEMV; the complete speed difference is not a causal shared-quantization estimate.
The initial operator benchmark, later semantic test, B1 binary, and final v2 binaries have separate hashes and validation scopes. Earlier device results do not automatically qualify v2.

Batch fixtures use identical token prompt [1,2,3,4] for 4 or 8 requests and teacher-forced continuation. 32/64 are eight-step per-request comparisons, not 32/64 independent prompts. Ragged prefill changes packing by pre-advancing half the requests, not prompt semantics.
Existing provider/native caches are reused. Cold means no selected decoder artifact; build time is excluded. Startup timings cannot be interpreted as controlled cold-JIT speedups.
Runtime arena sizes are not allocator peak, full VRAM, or service capacity. No maximum-capacity result is claimed.
Teacher-forced per-request logit checks are bounded numeric/state-lifecycle witnesses. They do not establish free-running text equality, diverse prompt coverage, or the failed/unrun ragged shapes.
B8 head eclass contains two cuBLASLt alternatives, but no same-shape device measurement or finalist-to-head mapping was preserved; the stage that lost these alternatives is undetermined.

The scratch lifecycle regression covers 24 tiny dynamic executions and two frozen replays, with exact old-owner lifetime assertions; it does not establish model throughput or arbitrary dynamic-shape coverage.
Package review is complete and promotion remains a separate root review action; historical failed experiments are retained.

Final v3 serving completed 32 measured requests, but two of eight generated texts differ between arms in both epochs. Exact-output equivalence remains unresolved; no independent oracle for these prompts supports a near-tie explanation.

The final serving schedule changes decode LM head and FP8 variant choices; on-decode has no multi-consumer shared quantizer. Whole-plan throughput/TPOT differences cannot be attributed solely to shared quantization.
First streaming gaps exceed subsequent intervals in all four serving runs. A one-materialized-bucket policy may contribute; client timing provides no per-stage causal attribution.

timing_definitions.comparison_limit: Existing native/provider caches reused. These are separate searched/load paths and include multiple preparation stages; not a controlled empty-cache JIT comparison.
timing_definitions.elapsed_process_seconds: Full prebuilt test subprocess, including test setup, decoder work, reference comparisons, diagnostic logits and drain; Rust build excluded.
timing_definitions.strict_replay_first_use_boundary: compile_or_load excludes later first-use shape preparation during prefill/decode. Restoring a selected schedule does not prove zero runtime setup/JIT for every live shape.
timing_definitions.test_marker_compile_seconds: Wall interval around the test compile_or_load_with_tuning invocation (including argument evaluation); covers decoder preparation/loading/search as performed by that call, not isolated compiler CPU time or Rust build time. Artifact JSON parsing occurs before this marker interval.
